verdict.rationale: OpenRouter documents programmatic API key creation and management, plus workspace budgets that cap spend over daily, weekly, monthly or lifetime intervals and automatically block requests once a limit is reached. A community user confirms per-key limits and expiry, so an agent can get its own capped key. However, first-party docs here describe budgets at the workspace level rather than per key, and no rate-limit guardrail is documented. Missing for 10: first-party docs for per-key spend limits, any documented per-key rate limiting, an explicit agent-key workflow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can give an autonomous agent its own key with budget and rate guardrails so it cannot run away on spend

citations.quote: OpenRouter provides endpoints to programmatically manage your API keys, enabling key creation and management for applications that need to distribute or rotate keys automatically.
Set a dollar limit on any combination of intervals — daily, weekly, monthly, or lifetime — and OpenRouter blocks requests automatically once a limit is reached.
One thing that OpenRouter makes easy is the ability to manage API keys (mint new ones, expiry/limits per key, etc.)
